note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §13.7, Stage 65; docs/CURRICULUM.md, experiment 19) on data/benches/antacid.json: an antacid by back titration. NaHCO3 + HCl -> NaCl + CO2 + H2O. An antacid tablet dissolves slowly and gives off a gas, so it is not titrated directly: it is given more acid than it can take, its carbon dioxide driven off, and the acid left over titrated.
title: Experiment: an antacid by back titration

report.label: the acid the tablet neutralised
report.why: 5.00 mmol of acid (25.00 mL of 0.200 M) less the base that met what was left (0.100 M times the burette's volume): each hydrogen carbonate takes one hydrogen ion. Had its carbon dioxide stayed, the base would have taken it too (as hydrogen carbonate, at phenolphthalein's end point), and the tablet would seem to have neutralised less.

report.label: what a gram of it neutralises
report.why: The acid it neutralised over the balance's reading of the tablet: sodium hydrogen carbonate, 84.007 g/mol, neutralises 11.9 mmol a gram.

steps.title: The flask on the balance
steps.text: Click the flask to pick it up, then click the balance. Then right-click the balance and click "tare".

checks.text: the flask tared on the balance

steps.title: The tablet
steps.text: Pick up the tablet's beaker, right-click the flask and click "tip the solid". Then right-click the balance and click "+ mass".

steps.title: 25 mL of the acid
steps.text: Pick up the pipette and click the hydrochloric acid: it draws to its mark. Then pick it up again and click the flask.
steps.why: 25.00 mL of 0.200 M is 5.00 mmol, more than a 0.35 g tablet can take (4.2 mmol): some is left over to titrate.

steps.title: Until it is empty
steps.text: Wait until the pipette has run out: the tablet fizzes.

steps.title: Swirled
steps.text: Pick up the pipette and click a free square. Right-click the flask, click "stir", and click 60x on the clock.

steps.title: Over a burner
steps.text: Click 1x. Pick up the flask and click its own place on the bench, off the balance. Then pick up the burner in Supplies and click the flask: it goes under it.

steps.title: Boil it
steps.text: Right-click the burner and drag its valve all the way open; click 60x.
steps.why: Carbon dioxide left in the flask, dissolved or in its air, would take some of the base at the end point, as hydrogen carbonate. Boiling drives it out: the steam carries it through the flask's mouth.

steps.title: Until its gas has gone
steps.text: Watch the flask boil until its carbon dioxide has gone.

steps.title: Let it cool
steps.text: Right-click the burner and shut its valve, then wait for the flask to cool.

steps.title: Phenolphthalein
steps.text: Click 1x. Pick up the phenolphthalein, right-click the flask, type 0.15 and click "pour".

steps.title: Fill the burette
steps.text: Pick up the potassium hydroxide, right-click the burette, type 55 and click "pour". Right-click the burette and click "+ mL". Then pick it up and click the flask.

steps.title: Drop by drop
steps.text: Right-click the burette, drag its tap to about 6 % and click 60x.
steps.why: What is left over is about 1 to 2 mmol: 8 to 20 mL of the base.

steps.title: The first lasting pink
steps.text: Watch the flask until it turns pink and stays pink.

steps.title: Shut it, and read it
steps.text: Drag the burette's tap shut, click 1x, then right-click the burette and click "+ mL".
